chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said:

"If the odd prayer (Witr) of your night is missed by you, then whenever you make it up the next day before midday, you have made it up as odd (Witr). And whenever you make it up at night, you have made it up as odd (Witr). And whenever you make it up during the day after that day, you make it up as even (Shaf'), adding another to it until it becomes even."
I said, 'And why was it made even?' He said, 'As a punishment for missing the odd (Witr).'
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And one does not make up a voluntary prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer.' This indicates that.

key_terms.الزَّوَالُ: Midday, when the sun begins to decline from its zenith
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: Making up a missed obligatory or recommended act
key_terms.وَتْرٌ: Odd prayer (Witr), specifically the odd-numbered night prayer

ai.seo_question: How should the missed Witr prayer be made up if not performed at night?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib details the specific compensatory mechanism for a missed Witr prayer, distinguishing between making it up as Witr if done before midday (Zawal) or as an even number (Shaf') if delayed, which serves as a disciplinary penalty for the omission. The inclusion of this ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the distinct status of Witr as a highly recommended (Mustahabb) act that retains its identity but incurs a structural change in its performance if missed. The concluding remark by Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that this makeup occurs outside the strict time window of the obligatory prayers, preserving the integrity of the Fard times.
